inspiration: Weapon as a data row: one script per weapon with a display-name key, models, ammo type, clip size, reserve, damage, a weapon-wheel bucket and position, and sound slots per event (single shot, double shot, reload, empty, special) (game/mod_hl2mp/scripts/weapon_ar2.txt:5-26 region). Each event has an NPC variant, so AI shots can be mixed without changing the player's sound.

HUD motion as a tiny script: one line animates a panel property (colour, position, size, alpha) to a target with a named easing (Linear, Accel, Deaccel); events can start or stop other events at a given time (game/mod_hl2mp/scripts/HudAnimations.txt:20-21 and the command comments).

Random ambience bed: a soundscape block picks a wave at random from a pool with a time range and a volume range, so ambience does not loop identically (game/mod_hl2mp/scripts/soundscapes_streetwar.txt:21 region).

Two-length labels: each item has a full-name key and a short menu key with a suffix, so the detail view and the narrow menu can each use the right length (game/mod_hl2mp/resource/mod_hl2mp_english.txt, key grammar only).
Two-line display names: some display names put a short parenthetical subtitle on a second line, which reads on a narrow screen (game/mod_hl2mp/resource/mod_hl2mp_english.txt, key grammar only).

briefs.label: Rifle with NPC shot variants
briefs.why: each shot type has its own sound, and the AI variant is separate so enemy fire can be tuned without touching the player's sound
briefs.keep: sound slot per event with an NPC variant
briefs.change: our own weapon and sound slots; no donor sound names; fewer fields per weapon row

briefs.label: Two-line weapon name
briefs.why: a short name plus a parenthetical subtitle reads without truncation on a phone

briefs.label: Random ambience bed
briefs.why: random pick with a time range and a volume range stops ambience reading as a loop
briefs.keep: interval range, volume range, wave pool
briefs.change: per-biome pools of our own sounds

briefs.label: Eased HUD motion vocabulary
briefs.why: three named curves cover most UI motion, and events can chain
briefs.change: a different curve set and our own hit-flash timing
